doc.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Driving to Las Vegas and Los Angeles, writing hard pieces
summary: Paul's trio got fired after two nights in Las Vegas, so they went to California, where she wrote difficult dissonant pieces that Scott LaFaro used as bass exercises.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So with you and Paul, the relationship was kindled there of course, with… in New York for how long before moving back to L.A.? And what?

Well that was just, Paul Bley wanted to move to LA, I don’t know why. Oh no, I think he went to, he wanted to go to Las Vegas. So he took his band, it was a trio, it was Lenny McBrown and Hal... Gaylor? And me, and we all got into Paul’s car and we drove to Las Vegas. And the gig only lasted two nights, and Paul got fired. So there we were in Las Vegas and we decided to go to California cause it was closer. It’s strange how you just can do anything you want to. You can decide to go North, South, East, West, it’s just wonderful. You don’t have anything holding you down, tying you down.
Were you starting to, did you start at that point to write for Paul, or that came once you’re in L.A.?

That came when I was in L.A. I wrote some really hard pieces like Donkey and... I wrote hard pieces... I don’t remember what their names are. But they are very dissonant, my mellow style had not developed yet. I was just a total... I’m not a good talker.
I don’t know a lot of words. What is it called when you have... they weren’t virtuosic, they didn’t... yes they did.

They really required virtuosity but I didn’t need it to write them cause I would think about each note very slowly. Come up with things that I thought were perfect and then Paul Bley would play them, or even Ned he would play them. Scott... what was the bass player’s name, Scott...
Scott LaFarro would come and pick them up and use them as exercises on the bass; he would play those things.
But he was just, he didn’t care about it musically, he just wanted to stretch his chops.
